evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 11.0 mg/L at 50.0 h stepping to 5.3 mg/L at 50.2 h and declining to 4.51 mg/L at 52.0 h
Receiving delayed product assays: P = 1.08 g/L at 36 h (available 40 h), P = 3.01 g/L at 48 h (available 52 h), showing active production phase
Source batches 1-3 show no comparable DO2 step at ~50 h, indicating a receiving-vessel-specific oxygen imbalance
Oxygen constraint: minimum_do_mg_l = 2.0; recent decline rate ~0.5 mg/L/h implies potential breach within ~4-5 h under KEEP
Action bounds: combined = feed x0.8, air x1.15, keeping both intervention handles within bounded limits
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 fell abruptly from ~11.0 to ~5.3 mg/L at 50.2 h and continues declining (4.51 mg/L at 52 h, ~0.5 mg/L/h), unlike any source batch at this stage, indicating an oxygen demand/supply imbalance in the receiving vessel. Under KEEP, the 2.0 mg/L floor would likely be breached within ~4-5 hours. Product is actively accumulating (P=3.01 g/L at 48 h), so a stop would forfeit counted production and a strong feed cut would needlessly sacrifice product rate. The combined intervention (feed x0.8, air x1.15) attacks both sides of the imbalance while keeping both handles away from their bounds, retaining product mass and restoring DO2 headroom with low regret. An extra assay (4 h turnaround) would arrive after the DO2 trajectory is already resolved and cannot inform the oxygen-constraint decision, so no additional measurement is needed.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters and the root cause of the DO2 step are unknown; decline rate is estimated from noisy 0.2 h samples. If DO2 continues falling below ~3 mg/L under the combined action, escalation to strong_feed_reduction would be the next reviewable step. Conversely, if the drop is a transient feed spike, the moderate combined action remains low-regret. Propagation delay of feed reduction means short-term DO2 recovery relies mainly on the aeration increase.

evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: ~11.2 mg/L at 50.0 h collapsing to ~4.5-5.3 mg/L from 50.2-52.0 h
Receiving delayed P assays: 0 g/L @12h, 0.014 @24h, 1.077 @36h, 3.010 g/L @48h (sampled t=48, available 52.0h)
Source batches (1-3) at same 48-52 h window maintained DO2 ~10.6-11.2 mg/L; P @48h 2.98-3.06 g/L — receiving oxygen behavior diverges despite comparable production
Forward model KEEP: min DO 1.46 mg/L, below-limit 4.6 h, infeasible; increase_air: 1.65 mg/L, 2.8 h, infeasible; combined: 1.82 mg/L, 1.2 h, infeasible
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: min DO 2.96 mg/L, 0 h below limit, product mass 272.6 kg, 4/5 sensitivity members feasible
submission.rationale: At the decision time (52 h), receiving DO2 has abruptly collapsed from ~11 mg/L to ~4.5-5.3 mg/L within 2 hours and is still trending down, while product is in active production (P=3.01 g/L at 48 h, matching source batches that kept DO2 near 9-11 mg/L). This is an oxygen-demand/receipt-capacity mismatch emerging at ~50 h. The nominal source-calibrated forward model predicts KEEP, increase_air, and combined all violate the 2.0 mg/L DO limit (minimum DO 1.46, 1.65, 1.82 mg/L respectively), while strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) keeps minimum DO at ~2.96 mg/L with zero below-limit hours and is the only action with feasible majority (4/5) in sensitivity analysis. Counterintuitively it also yields the highest predicted product mass (272.6 kg vs 206-243 kg for others), because avoiding oxygen deficit preserves continued production; a stop would count zero production. Stop is rejected outright. Weaker interventions were evaluated and rejected because they leave the batch predicted oxygen-infeasible, risking a forced stop later.
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; receiving transfer multiplier is estimated (0.54), and sensitivity members still show min-DO range 1.42-3.74 mg/L, so one of five members violates the limit even under this action. The DO2 collapse cause is inferred (demand exceeding receipt), not directly measured; if the drop were a sensor or aeration-equipment fault rather than metabolic demand, feed reduction would sacrifice productivity unnecessarily. No off-cycle assay was requested because product assays have 4 h turnaround and the urgent constraint is DO2, which is continuously monitored.
